title: Solve ax^2 + c = 0 with the principle of square roots

section.book: Bittinger, Beecher, Ellenbogen & Penna, College Algebra: Graphs and Models, 7e
section.title: Quadratic Equations, Functions, Zeros, and Models

process_card: Solving with the principle of square roots

steps.name: take the square root of both sides (plus or minus)
simplify the radical (use i if the number is negative)

mistakes.name: forgot ±
mistakes.message: x^2 = k has two solutions: write ± in front of the root.

mistakes.name: forgot i
mistakes.message: The square root of a negative number is imaginary: sqrt(-7) = sqrt(7) i.

hints.hint: Undo the constant first, then divide by the coefficient of x^2.
hints.why: The principle of square roots needs x^2 alone: x^2 = k.

hints.step: take the square root of both sides (plus or minus)
hints.hint: Write x = ± the square root of the number.
hints.why: A number and its opposite both square to k.

hints.step: simplify the radical (use i if the number is negative)
hints.hint: Pull out square factors; a negative under the root becomes i.
hints.why: Exact answers are written with simplified radicals and i.

hints.hint: Square your answer and substitute it back.
hints.why: Squaring catches a lost i or a wrong radical.
